newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn falls to new contract lows, two-yr lows.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn falls to new contract lows, two-yr lows.

text.p: CBOT corn futures sank to new contract lows and fresh two-year lows on recent near-perfect crop weather in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
"That's base level but clearly something is going on in old crop too," said Dave Armstrong, Chicago-based analyst for trade house ABN Amro Chicago Corp of the weather impact on corn futures Thursday.
The new low for July is $2.50 a bushel, below the previous low of $2.55-3/4 set Wednesday. The low also is the lowest for a nearby contract since May 1995 when the nearby touched $2.48.
Corn closed one to six cents lower, with July down six at $2.50-1/4 and December closed three cents lower at $2.39-1/4.

Wednesday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook was for normal temperatures and above normal precipitation through the U.S. Corn Belt from July 1 through July 5. Also, USDA on Monday said the U.S. crop as of Sunday was 67 percent good to excellent.
Armstrong said end users now were in no hurry to buy old crop corn as it appears a bumper crop will be harvested this fall.

"It's just kind of a spongy demand for old crop now," he said. "The demand side is pretty well covered and if you look at the export sales every week we're not doing much plus Japan is pretty well covered," he said.
